html:
The Wangunk, also called the Mattabesec, were a group of closely related Algonquian peoples of central Connecticut, along the Connecticut River around today's Middletown and Wethersfield. Many writers count them as part of the Wappinger confederacy.

They farmed maize on the rich river meadows and fished the river. In the 1630s English settlers from Massachusetts founded towns on their land, and the Wangunk sachem Sowheag clashed with the settlers of Wethersfield in the years around the Pequot War of 1637. Over the following century they sold or lost most of their land, and their last members joined other Native communities, such as the Mohegan and the Brothertown movement. Their western neighbours were the Paugussett.
